planned_arc.note: Pre-locked season-1 finale arc EP6-EP15. Scenarist follows this as RAILS: keep the locked key_lines and cliffhanger lines verbatim (translate only if language != en), adapt each episode's beats into 3-5 clips under serial-drama constraints (max 2 chars per frame, I2V = micro-motion only, all movement/explosions/pod-flight = CUT between clips not animation, protagonist always faces camera, cliffhanger spoken line = Avatar TTS). After shipping an episode, fold its loops/status into characters[], active_loops, episode_summaries as usual. Do NOT re-invent episodes while this arc has unshipped entries.

new_characters.name: Mirror Kirk
new_characters.character_description: semi-realistic Pixar 3D mirror-universe James T. Kirk, identical face to Kirk but harder and predatory, cold confident smirk, thin scar across one cheek, slicked darker hair, dead-calm eyes, black-and-silver Section 31 mirror uniform with sharp trim instead of gold command tunic
new_characters.voice_note: Same voice as Kirk BY DESIGN (he is a mirror double) - differentiate via lower stability / colder delivery, not a different voice.

episodes.title: 11 Seconds
episodes.link: EP5 ended on timer 00:11 and the Admiral's order to fire on the allied ship.
beats: Bridge. Timer 00:11. Allied ship locked in the targeting reticle.
Admiral demands Kirk fire - the ship is 'quarantined'.
Kirk refuses; orders Scotty to overload Enterprise's own phaser node.
Enterprise phaser array blows, the shot is aborted.
A black pod launches from the damaged allied ship and races toward Enterprise.

key_lines.speaker: Admiral
key_lines.line: Captain, that ship must not survive.

key_lines.speaker: Kirk
key_lines.line: Then you should have told me why.

key_lines.speaker: Scotty
key_lines.line: We'll lose the phasers!

key_lines.speaker: Kirk
key_lines.line: Better the weapons than my conscience.

cliffhanger.scene: The pod slams into the Enterprise hangar/airlock. Scanner reads a biosignature.

loops: why the Admiral wanted the ship destroyed

episodes.title: The Man in the Pod
episodes.link: The Kirk-biosignature pod reached the ship because Kirk chose not to fire.
beats: Airlock. The pod is smoking, red alert all around.
Kirk, Worf, Spock and Chekov approach it.
Admiral on the viewscreen orders: do not open it, jettison the pod into space.
Kirk orders it opened manually.
Mirror Kirk steps out of the pod.

key_lines.speaker: Admiral
key_lines.line: Do not open it. That is a direct order.

key_lines.speaker: Kirk
key_lines.line: You already lied to me once.

key_lines.speaker: Chekov
key_lines.line: I saw that pod before the airlock.

key_lines.speaker: Mirror Kirk
key_lines.line: Hello, Jim. You're late again.

cliffhanger.scene: Mirror Kirk looks at Chekov and smiles.
cliffhanger.line: And that one was supposed to die first.

loops: why Chekov was led to the airlock

episodes.title: First Blood
episodes.link: Mirror Kirk ties himself directly to the first attempt to kill Chekov.
beats: Corridor by the airlock. Worf tries to detain Mirror Kirk.
Mirror Kirk provokes Worf and slips the grab.
Kirk shields Chekov with his own body.
Mirror Kirk drops a black Section 31 token on the floor.
The token shows an order with the Admiral's signature, tagged AIRLOCK TEST SUBJECT: CHEKOV.

key_lines.speaker: Worf
key_lines.line: Take one step and I'll break your neck.

key_lines.speaker: Mirror Kirk
key_lines.line: You're slower than my Worf.

key_lines.speaker: Kirk
key_lines.line: Why Chekov?

key_lines.speaker: Mirror Kirk
key_lines.line: Because you'll always save the boy.

cliffhanger.scene: The token reactivates the old order. The airlock door opens again.

loops: the airlock was a test OF Kirk
the Admiral knew about the double

episodes.title: The Test
episodes.link: Mirror Kirk's token restarted the Airlock Protocol.
beats: Airlock opens. Decompression drags Chekov toward it.
Kirk grabs Chekov's hand. Worf holds Kirk.
Mirror Kirk stands calmly nearby and does not help.
Spock at the panel sees: the protocol isn't killing Chekov, it's measuring Kirk's reaction.
Kirk saves Chekov, but the system logs: KIRK FAILED COMMAND THRESHOLD.

key_lines.speaker: Chekov
key_lines.line: Captain, I can't hold on!

key_lines.speaker: Kirk
key_lines.line: Look at me!

key_lines.speaker: Mirror Kirk
key_lines.line: That's why they chose you.

key_lines.speaker: Spock
key_lines.line: This is not an execution. It's an examination.

cliffhanger.scene: The test result appears on screen.

loops: Mirror Kirk is the replacement candidate
Kirk 'failed' the test through his humanity

episodes.title: Replacement Captain
episodes.link: The system accepted Mirror Kirk as a suitable replacement.
beats: Bridge. Kirk's captain access is locked out.
Mirror Kirk gets temporary access to the tactical panel.
He doesn't fire at once - he shows he can 'save' the situation faster.
Scotty proves his code wasn't used for betrayal but to prep a captain swap.
Mirror Kirk gives his first order: turn the ship against the Admiral.

key_lines.speaker: Mirror Kirk
key_lines.line: Your fleet wants a captain who'll push the button.

key_lines.speaker: Kirk
key_lines.line: Cowards push buttons.

key_lines.speaker: Scotty
key_lines.line: My code didn't open the weapons. It opened the captain's chair.

key_lines.speaker: Spock
key_lines.line: Section 31 wasn't building a trap. They were building a replacement.

cliffhanger.scene: Mirror Kirk now aims not at the allies but at the Admiral's ship.
cliffhanger.line: Now I'll save you my way.

loops: the Admiral is no longer the only enemy

episodes.title: Bad Rescue
episodes.link: Mirror Kirk wants to destroy the Admiral, but that too is a war crime.
beats: Bridge. Weapons trained on the Admiral's ship.
The real Kirk demands they stand down.
Mirror Kirk argues it's the only way to save the crew.
Worf is caught between two Kirks: one morally right, one tactically right.
Spock disables targeting, but Mirror Kirk launches a torpedo manually.

key_lines.speaker: Kirk
key_lines.line: We don't execute people without a trial.

key_lines.speaker: Mirror Kirk
key_lines.line: While you judge, they kill.

key_lines.speaker: Worf
key_lines.line: Both speak of honor. One smells of blood.

key_lines.speaker: Spock
key_lines.line: His logic is efficient. That is why it's dangerous.

cliffhanger.scene: The torpedo launches. The Admiral loses his composure for the first time.

loops: Mirror Kirk isn't just evil, he's effective
the Admiral fears not death but consequences

episodes.title: Stop the Torpedo
episodes.link: The torpedo is already in flight; now they must stop the disaster Mirror Kirk created.
beats: Engineering. Scotty tries to intercept the torpedo.
Bridge. Kirk takes the ship into a dangerous maneuver.
Worf manually fires on their own torpedo.
The torpedo is shot down, but the blast damages both ships.
The damage costs the Admiral his Section 31 protected channel.

key_lines.speaker: Scotty
key_lines.line: I can stop it, but it'll burn our shields.

key_lines.speaker: Kirk
key_lines.line: Burn them.

key_lines.speaker: Mirror Kirk
key_lines.line: You'd save even your enemies. It's a disease.

key_lines.speaker: Kirk
key_lines.line: No. It's the Federation.

cliffhanger.scene: The Admiral's signal is traced - he's not on a base, he's aboard the allied ship.
cliffhanger.line: The Admiral was there the whole time.

loops: the allied ship was a prison

episodes.title: The Admiral on Board
episodes.link: It turns out the Admiral was hiding on the very allied ship he ordered destroyed.
beats: Viewscreen. The allied ship is damaged; the Admiral's private cabin is visible.
The Admiral admits: the ship was carrying Mirror Kirk as a secret asset.
Chekov remembers: he saw the transport manifest, which is why he was being removed.
Kirk demands the Admiral be handed over for trial.
Mirror Kirk offers a simpler route: finish off the ship and end it all.

key_lines.speaker: Admiral
key_lines.line: I protected the Federation from your mercy.

key_lines.speaker: Kirk
key_lines.line: You protected yourself from witnesses.

key_lines.speaker: Chekov
key_lines.line: I saw the name on the manifest. James Kirk.

key_lines.speaker: Mirror Kirk
key_lines.line: A trial is just deferred cowardice.

cliffhanger.scene: The Admiral triggers self-destruct of all evidence on both ships.

loops: new disaster: destruction of the evidence

episodes.title: No Witnesses
episodes.link: The Admiral starts self-destruct to erase himself, the double, and all evidence.
beats: Bridge. Self-destruct timer counting down.
Engineering. Scotty tries to save the logs.
Mirror Kirk unexpectedly helps - not out of good, but because he won't die as someone's asset.
The real Kirk is forced to work alongside him in the same frame.
Together they shut down one circuit, but the second needs a captain's sacrifice.

key_lines.speaker: Mirror Kirk
key_lines.line: I won't die as someone else's instrument.

key_lines.speaker: Kirk
key_lines.line: Then for once, make your own choice.

key_lines.speaker: Scotty
key_lines.line: The logs are uploading to the fleet. But the timer just sped up.

key_lines.speaker: Spock
key_lines.line: One of you has to stay at the core.

cliffhanger.scene: Mirror Kirk stays at the core. He closes the door on the real Kirk.
cliffhanger.line: Don't thank me. I'm still better than you.

episodes.title: The Airlock Choice
episodes.link: Mirror Kirk stayed at the core to stop the self-destruct.
beats: Engineering. Mirror Kirk holds the overload manually.
Bridge. The real Kirk broadcasts the evidence to the entire fleet.
The Admiral tries to jam the signal with a mutiny order.
Chekov confirms the manifest and the Airlock Protocol.
Mirror Kirk aborts the self-destruct, but vanishes into a mirror rift.

key_lines.speaker: Kirk
key_lines.line: The fleet shouldn't hear an order. They should hear the truth.

key_lines.speaker: Chekov
key_lines.line: They tried to kill me over that name.

key_lines.speaker: Admiral
key_lines.line: You'll destroy trust in the command.

key_lines.speaker: Kirk
key_lines.line: No. You already did.

cliffhanger.scene: SEASON CLIFF: Evidence accepted, Admiral arrested. Final shot - an identical black pod opens on another ship.
cliffhanger.line: The first Kirk never came back.

loops: OPEN for season 2: the Mirror network

planned_arc.mirror_kirk_survival_note: Mirror Kirk was accidentally ejected through the airlock in EP8. He survived — Section 31 recovered him via emergency shuttle (off-screen). He reappears unexpectedly around EP11-12, referencing the incident: 'I've been outside before.' The arc continues but with the knowledge that Mirror Kirk is harder to kill than expected.

episode_summaries.summary: Worf leads Chekov to the airlock on Fleet Admiral's orders. Kirk commands Worf to stand down — refused. Worf claims the order was signed personally by the Fleet Admiral. Kirk and Worf watch the airlock seal. Chekov screams it's a setup from behind the glass. Kirk asks: 'Worf. Who really gave you that order.' Worf drops his eyes. Silence.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Worf knows who really gave the order — and it wasn't the Fleet Admiral

episode_summaries.summary: Worf breaks silence — reveals Section 31 gave the kill order. Kirk denies it ('That's a ghost story'). Worf produces PADD with Fleet Admiral's personal seal. Kirk goes ice-cold: 'The order. Show me.' Worf: 'Now you see, Captain. We are both dead.' The airlock door SWITCHES from SEALED to UNLOCKED by itself — nobody touched it. Kirk and Worf both stare.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Someone has remote control of the ship. Nobody authorized the unlock. The door is open.

episode_summaries.summary: Worf grabs Kirk — warns the watcher is still active. Kirk walks through anyway: 'Then they're watching me walk through it.' Worf draws phaser, holds the doorway. Kirk finds Chekov alive inside the airlock chamber, slumped against the wall. Chekov delivers his bombshell: 'it's someone on your crew.' Behind them: Worf spots a silhouette figure at the far corridor junction — motionless, arm raised, pointing at Kirk. Worf's phaser swings toward it. Standoff.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: A figure in Starfleet uniform stands at the corridor end pointing at Kirk. It doesn't move. It doesn't run. Who is the mole — and is this figure ally or assassin?

episode_summaries.summary: The watcher walks forward into the red alert light — it's Spock. Worf lowers his phaser. Spock tells Kirk the weapons array was armed six minutes ago and Scotty is on the bridge. Two minutes left. Kirk orders Worf to guard Chekov and sprints alone toward the bridge.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Exterior shot: Enterprise weapons array locks on an allied Starfleet escort vessel. Amber targeting reticle confirmed. Kirk is still running.

episode_summaries.summary: Kirk bursts onto the bridge in time. Scotty is at the weapons console but claims he was locked out — someone has remote access. The weapons array stays locked on the allied vessel. Then the viewscreen activates: the Fleet Admiral appears, calm and watching. He says one word.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Fleet Admiral appears on viewscreen — "Captain." Countdown at 00:11.

episode_summaries.summary: Admiral orders Kirk to fire on the allied ship with 11 seconds left. Kirk refuses. He overloads Enterprise's own phaser array — weapons destroyed, shot aborted. A black pod launches from the damaged allied ship and crashes into the Enterprise airlock. Spock wipes the porthole glass and sees Kirk's face inside the pod.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Biosignature scanner reads JAMES T. KIRK — ALIVE. Spock: 'Captain... it's you in there.' Kirk is standing right there.

episode_summaries.summary: Kirk, Worf, Spock and Chekov stand before the smoking black pod in the airlock. The Admiral appears on the comm panel and orders them not to open it: 'Do not open it. That is a direct order.' Kirk refuses: 'You already lied to me once.' Chekov recognizes the pod — 'I saw that pod before the airlock.' Kirk manually cranks the hatch open. Mirror Kirk — identical face, scar on cheek, black-silver Section 31 uniform — steps out of the smoke and says: 'Hello, Jim. You're late again.'
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Mirror Kirk turns slowly toward Chekov with a predatory smile: 'And that one was supposed to die first.' Chekov freezes.

episode_summaries.summary: Mirror Kirk steps free of the pod. Worf tries to grab him — Mirror Kirk slips the hold. Kirk steps between Mirror Kirk and Chekov. Mirror Kirk reveals Chekov was always the target: 'Because you'll always save the boy.' Then Mirror Kirk presses the LCARS emergency panel — the outer airlock door cracks open behind Chekov. Explosive decompression drags Chekov toward the gap; he grabs the door frame and holds on. Mirror Kirk is also pulled out through the gap he opened.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Chekov hanging on the airlock frame, stars behind him. Mirror Kirk ejected into space.
